reader.notes: The 1985 rule has an arm of its own. ResolveReports looks each operand up, then ScreenControlItemsDistinct compares the RESOLVED DataItem objects with ReferenceEquals; the 2002+ written-reference loop is off below 2002. The probes refuse one item spelled two ways at 85 and accept it at 2023, as each edition's text requires.
reader.at-2023: ctlqual compiles and runs (different, and correct for 2023 SR6)

refuter.evidence: At --std 85: ctlmulti (CONTROLS ARE CX OF WG OF REC CX OF REC, one item) gives COBOL1699 citing §1985:XIII.3.7.3 SR2, exit 65. ctlfin (FINAL CX CZ CX OF WG, with a non-adjacent repeat) gives COBOL1699, exit 65. ctl2grp (CX OF WG1 CX OF WG2, two items with one name) exit 0, OK. So the resolved-item comparison is right. The case the reader did not try is ctlren: 01 WG with 05 CX and 05 CZ, then 66 RX RENAMES CX, and CONTROLS ARE CX RX. It CRASHES: exit 1, 'Unhandled exception: System.InvalidOperationException: no Place was built for data item 'RX' when binding finished' (PlaceTable.Of via PlaceTablePass.TableOf). ctlren1 (CONTROLS ARE RX alone) crashes the same way. ctlren0 (RX declared, CONTROLS ARE CX) exit 0, OK. ctlren at --std 2023 crashes identically, so the cause is (b). A level-66 name is a data-name, and OK §1985:XIII.3.7.3 SR1 'Data-name-1 must not be defined in the Report Section' is SR1's only bar on the operand. The RENAMES is legal (OK §1985:VI.5.11.3 SR4 'must be names of elementary items or groups of elementary items'). RX is its own entry with CX's attributes (OK §1985:VI.5.11.4 GR2). Reading: RX and CX are different data items (the same storage, like the REDEFINES pair the reader accepted), so OK §1985:XIII.3.7.3 SR2 'Each recurrence of data-name-1 must identify a different data item' admits CX RX, and the compiler crashes instead of compiling it. Under the opposite reading (one item) SR2 refuses it, and the compiler crashes instead of refusing. Either way this operand class gets no SR2 verdict. The crash is in the CONTROL operand's place building (PlaceTablePass), not in ScreenControlItemsDistinct. That is why I mark this DOUBTFUL rather than OVERTURNED. No kb/Work note found (searched kb/Work for RENAMES together with CONTROL operand/clause; PB2375 is only the extraction the message names).
refuter.corrected: SR2's resolved-item arm (ScreenControlItemsDistinct) is right for every operand that binds. A level-66 RENAMES operand crashes the compile at every edition (harm: crashes, cause b), so this rule has no verdict for that operand class. File it as a new defect against the CONTROL operand path (ReportSectionBinder.ResolveReports, then PlaceTablePass).
